I make sure my clients understand that no matter what the producer has led us to believe about the segment, chances are it’s going to play out completely opposite, and in working with the media, you have to be ready for anything. At “CBS This Morning,” the producer followed my client from the time he walked into the building, to the makeup chair, to when he went on the air, grilling him on the subject and making sure he knew the latest developments. He explained to Herring the specific direction the anchors were going to take, but it never played out as planned. The anchors ran off with the show. At CNN, my client was told various hit times—that is, the times he would “hit” the air—and most of them were moved forward or back. He was told he would be on camera for various lengths of time, but each hit went much longer or shorter than what he was told as the story developed. 4. I encourage my clients to say something different, take the other side of an issue, and not to be afraid to be controversial, but of course, they better be able to back it up. With the Carnival Triumph, Herring believed that people should not sue the cruise line. He insisted a cruise ship consists of thousands of moving pieces and parts and these things happen. The statue was erected at Delphi in 478 or 474 BC, to commemorate the victory of a chariot team in the Pythian Games, which were held at Delphi every four years in honor of Pythean Apollo. It was originally part of a larger group of statuary, including the chariot, four (possibly six) horses and two grooms. Some fragments of the horses were found with the statue. When intact, it must have been one of the most imposing works in ancient Greece. The Charioteer stands as a testament to both athletic excellence and artistic skill from over 2000 years ago; its intricate detailing showcases not only technical proficiency but also an understanding of movement and anatomy. The statue's portrayal captures what appears to be the moment immediately after victory, with tension evident in every line. The figure is dressed simply—a short chiton reveals musculature beneath while a cloak draped over one shoulder adds both decoration as well as realism; it suggests motion yet provides insight into ancient Greek clothing. The helmet lacks any facial features and has holes for ventilation on the sides, indicating its functionality in sport rather than battle. The Charioteer of Delphi was not just an individual victory but a symbol representing larger themes such as athletic competition, dedication to gods (the games were held at sanctuaries dedicated specifically), community spirit among athletes who trained together and competed for honor. The statue serves both commemorative purpose in the athlete's triumphs; it also stands today as one of history’s enduring witnesses—a silent but eloquent testament to a time when sports played an integral role not just within Greek society, or any culture. This remarkable artifact continues to captivate and inspire modern audiences with its timeless depiction of human achievement. In contrast, no fluorescence quenching was observed when using a neutrally charged peptide, poly-l-lysine hydrochloride (a positively charged peptide), or poly-l-aspartic acid sodium salt (a negatively charged peptide).
